name: Brachyolmia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Brachyolmia

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short trunk dwarfism with relatively normal limb length
Radiological evidence of platyspondyly (flattened vertebral bodies) on spinal imaging
Narrowed interpedicular distance in the lumbar spine on imaging
Mild facial dysmorphic features such as midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate short trunk dwarfism plus radiological evidence of platyspondyly and narrowed interpedicular distance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Narrowed interpedicular distance in lumbar spine
searchTerms: reduced spinal canal width in lower back
slight inward curve of lower back

common.symptomName: Short stature with normal limb proportions
searchTerms: short height with normal limb size
normal limb proportions with short body

common.symptomName: Mild facial dysmorphism including midface hypoplasia

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications due to spinal canal stenosis
searchTerms: neurological issues due to spinal stenosis
spinal canal pressure causing nerve symptoms

rare.symptomName: Respiratory compromise secondary to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from chest cage abnormalities
lung problems due to chest shape

imaging: Narrowed interpedicular distance in lumbar vertebrae
Mild scoliosis or kyphosis on spinal imaging
genetic: Mutations in the PAPSS2 gene (in some cases)
other: Normal limb length relative to trunk shortening

distinguishingFeatures: More severe short stature with both trunk and limb involvement
Disproportionate short stature with short limbs
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic cage deformity
Rapidly worsening spinal deformities causing functional impairment
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Brachyolmia. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.

Warman ML, Cormier-Daire V, Hall C, Krakow D, Lachman R, LeMerrer M, Mortier G, Rimoin DL, Savarirayan R, Sillence D. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2010 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2011 Jun;155A(5):943-68.
